review_candidates.title: Customer Account Manager
review_candidates.description: Chi siamo Geven è un'azienda leader a livello globale nel settore aeronautico. Con un impegno costante verso l'innovazione e la qualità, progettiamo e produciamo poltrone ed interni per aerei , garantendo un'esperienza di volo superiore per milioni di passeggeri. La nostra forza risiede nella passione per il nostro lavoro e nella capacità di adattarci alle sfide del futuro, rendendoci un punto di riferimento nel settore. Chi cerchiamo e cosa farai Per potenziare la nostra struttura commerciale, ricerchiamo un/una Customer Account Manager con consolidata esperienza nella gestione di clienti internazionali nel settore aeronautico o in ambiti industriali altamente tecnologici. La risorsa, riportando alla Direzione Commerciale, sioccuperà della fidelizzazione e del monitoraggio operativo delle commesse aeronautiche già acquisite, garantendo il rispetto dei massimi standard di qualità e dei tempi di consegna. Le principali responsabilità includono: - Analizzare le richieste del cliente e verificarne gli impatti tecnici, economici e produttivi. - Gestire le richieste di modifica del prodotto e coordinare la relativa valutazione con Engineering, Operations, Quality e le altre funzioni aziendali. - Preparare quotazioni, offerte commerciali e offerte relative a modifiche di prodotto. - Analizzare RFQ, specifiche del cliente e requisiti commerciali. - Valutare costi di sviluppo, certificazione, materiali, attrezzature e produzione con il supporto delle funzioni aziendali. - Consolidamento delle relazioni commerciali con clienti internazionali, costruttori OEM e compagnie aeree; -Gestione e monitoraggio operativo delle commesse aeronautiche già acquisite, garantendo il rispetto dei massimi standard di qualità e dei tempi di consegna. - Collaborazione costante con le funzioni interne (Program Management, Engineering, Legal, Operations) per garantire l’allineamento tecnico e contrattuale con le esigenze del cliente; -Monitoraggio del mercato e dei competitor per individuare trend, rischi e opportunità strategiche; -Partecipazione a fiere di settore, meeting e missioni commerciali in ambito internazionale. Competenze richieste Per avere successo in questo ruolo, avrai bisogno di: · Diploma tecnico (Meccanico/Aeronautico) o Laurea in Ingegneria (Gestionale, Meccanica, Aerospaziale) o background equivalente. · 3-7 anni di esperienza nella gestione tecnica del cliente all’l'interno di aziende metalmeccaniche complesse (la provenienza dal settore Aerospace costituisce un forte plus).  · Eccellenti capacità di negoziazione e gestione contrattuale in ambito internazionale; · Ottima conoscenza della lingua inglese (livello minimo B2, scritto e parlato); la conoscenza di una seconda lingua straniera costituisce un plus; · Ottima padronanza degli strumenti informatici e dei principali software gestionali (CRM, ERP); · Standing professionale elevato, orientamento ai risultati e forte attitudine alle relazioni interpersonali; · Disponibilità ad eventuali trasferte internazionali; · Spirito imprenditoriale, capacità di analisi e approccio strategico al business. Cosa offriamo Un ambiente internazionale, dinamico e stimolante, in cui la professionalità e la competenza rappresentano valori fondamentali. La posizione offre un’elevata visibilità all’interno dell’organizzazione, interfacciandosi con i principali stakeholder aziendali e con i top player del settore aeronautico globale. L'azienda promuove le pari opportunità e si impegna a garantire un ambiente di lavoro inclusivo e rispettoso della diversità. Incoraggiamo l'invio di candidature da parte di persone appartenenti a tutte le categorie protette, inclusi individui con disabilità, in conformità con la normativa vigente (L.68/99). Contratto di lavoro: Tempo pieno RAL : 38.000/42.000 euro in base alle pregresse esperienze del candidato; Contratto di lavoro: Tempo pieno Benefit: Mensa aziendale Istruzione: Laurea triennale (Preferenziale) Sede di lavoro: In Presenza

review_candidates.title: Cultural Mediator (Arabic)
review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates. Organizational Context and Scope Responsibilities Under the general supervision of the Chief of Mission, and the direct supervision of the National Project Officer, the Cultural Mediator , is responsible for the following duties and responsibilities: Provide interpretation and cultural mediation to migrants for effective communication between IOM staff and beneficiaries, including during individual/group sessions, field activities, transportation movements, and other relevant project implementation activities. Keep and respect the professional confidentiality. Develop and maintain good relations with the beneficiaries, relevant stakeholders and other humanitarian actors to support adequate implementation and coordination of project activities. Support in translating information materials/documents and other needed information used for individual and/ or group activities with beneficiaries. Facilitate communication, through interpretation and/or translation, in a spoken or written language understood by the beneficiaries, between the beneficiaries and the staff, in an objective and impartial way. Perform other duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education High school degree/ certificate with minimum three years of work experience; or University degree from an accredited academic institution with one year of relevant experience is an advantage. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience And Skills Previous work experience in a similar role ; Process adequate combination of knowledge, education, training experience to perform essential functions of the position; Experience in working in a multi-cultural environment preferred; Process adequate skills to perform essential functions of the position; Computer literacy in standard software applications; Strong work ethics and commitment to humanitarian principles; Valid driver’s license. Languages All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish). For this position, fluency in Arabic and English (oral and written) is required. Knowledge of Greek, French, Farsi or any other IOM official language is an advantage. Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 1 Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty. Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction. Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings. Notes Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances. IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts. IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here ). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

review_candidates.title: Country Director for Ukraine
review_candidates.description: People in Need (PIN) is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has provided humanitarian and development assistance across more than 40 countries since 1992. Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad. Contract Length: 2 years Country Programme: Ukraine Based: Kyiv Starting date: 3Q 2026 Line Manager: Regional Director for Eastern Europe and Afghanistan About The Ukrainian Programme Of People In Need People in Need (PIN) began operations in Ukraine in 2003 with human rights programs and expanded to humanitarian assistance in 2014. With the full-scale invasion in February 2022, we significantly scaled up our programming across the country. Since then, PIN has reached almost 4 million people, working through a network of local partner organizations. Today, PIN has its offices and teams in 8 oblasts in Ukraine with more than 500 local and international staff working in Lvivska, Kyivska (head office), Sumska, Kharkivska, Dnipropetrovska, Mykolaivska and Khersonska, Zaporizka, and Donetska oblasts. PIN's assistance addresses both immediate and longer-term needs of war-affected people, focusing on safe water and sanitation, shelter repairs, protection services, and education in emergencies. Our recovery programming delivers more systemic solutions, including support to district heating systems and renewable energy initiatives. PIN also provides comprehensive assistance to veterans and their families, including business grants and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), strengthens the quality of education in schools, and advances systemic improvements in social care for the most vulnerable. Funding comes from a diverse range of institutional and private donors. About the role: Country Director (CD) will provide leadership and management to country program team and oversee program quality and program development. CD will represent PIN to donors and will ensure coordination with relevant local stakeholders and partners. Main Duties & Responsibilities: Senior Management and Strategic Planning Represent PIN at national level, and be responsible for strategic leadership of the country programme; Overall supervision of the program implementation and regular updates of PIN Ukraine Country Programme Strategy; Lead the Senior Management Team, and oversee coordination of the whole country programme. Project Development and Representation Oversee program and project development in line with country programs strategy and Relief and Development Department strategy; Network and position PIN with donors and key stakeholders to actively seek funding opportunities, help to increase the quality of proposals, understand donor priorities and ensure coordination; Represent PIN at meetings with government partners, regional and local authorities, donors, local civil society, other INGOs, coordination bodies and other relevant stakeholders. Human Resource Management Plan HR needs, capacity building needs for senior staff and ensure sufficient human resources. Line management of senior team members including Deputy Country Director for Programs, Deputy Country Director for Systems and Operations, Head of MEAL, Risk Management Director and Communication and Advocacy Director; Monitor implementation of key policies to ensure equality and diversity within the team; Support, motivate and consult the country programme’s staff. Quality & Risk Management Ensures that procedures described in PIN policies, including the Safeguarding Policy, are in place and functional; Ensures that all support departments and functions are in place; Sets up effective internal coordination and communication; Ensures the high quality of submitted proposals; according to the size and structure of the country programme; Approves project proposals, contracts and payments according to given thresholds; Manages the most important risks and coordinates risk mitigation measure; Ensures PIN works in line with international Social and Environmental standards; Ensures compliance with PIN Data Protection Policy; Protects PIN from any reputational risks. Safety & Security Adhering to the PIN Safety and Security Policy and country-relevant procedures; Strives for the maximum safety and security of PIN’s staff and assets and ensures an awareness of risks and mitigation strategies; Ensures a balance between the accepted level of risk and the urgency of programmes (as per the Risk Management Policy); Executes crisis management; leads the Incident Management Team (IMT). Ensures that the Do-no-harm approach and maximum protection of PIN’s beneficiaries is applied. Security situation in Ukraine: Humanitarian workers continue to operate throughout Ukraine, although the front-line areas are being shelled almost constantly, and main cities are being targeted with missiles and UAVs quite regularly. PIN security SOPs require PIN staff to proceed to shelter should the risk level be assessed by the Security Department as the highest (launch of missiles or drones) and remain there until the air raid siren is cancelled, which cumulatively can be as often as every day, occasionally for several hours at a time (although shorter periods are as well occurring). Even though air strikes target military, energy and water infrastructure, it is often that the strikes are highly inaccurate and hit civilian infrastructure en masse. Strikes aren’t exclusive to the frontline areas and cover to different extent all the regions of Ukraine. Ukrainian air defence capabilities are severely depleted by lack of missiles provided by western allies, hence a significant number of missiles and drones reach their targets. Outside of the areas in the vicinity to the contact line, services such as medical care, shops, public transportation as well as restaurants or leisure facilities remain operational. Requirements: Significant previous experience with managing finance, logistics and procurement and HR in humanitarian, recovery or development setting; Experience with team management and supervision, and interest in building staff capacity; Experience of working in a humanitarian and/or development organization, including in developing and delivering processes/procedures and policies compliant with main international donors (previous experience with ECHO, NDICI, US Government or UN is an asset); Excellent communication skills, fluent spoken and written English; IT literacy, advanced knowledge of MS Excel; Strong coordination, critical analysis and problem-solving skills; Responsible and systematic, and ability to organize and plan effectively; Ownership, independence, proactive approach, flexibility; Ability to work in difficult conditions and under pressure; Ukrainian language is an advantage. We offer: Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context; Strategic role with direct contribution to PIN’s funding diversification; Close collaboration with senior leadership in a country programme; Salary & Benefits: Salary based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies; expected salary range between 4200 - 4400 EUR super gross based on experience, Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR/month; Hardship of 400 EUR/month; Housing Allowance of 1000 EUR/month; RnR allowance of 300 EUR/cycle. Time off and Rest: 25 days of holiday annually; 10 sick days 5 days of RnR up to three cycles per calendar year Travel benefits: Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work; Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure; Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment; Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation. Health and Well-being: 24/7 Medical Support available online; Free psychological consultations available online Professional Development: Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities, including Hostile Environment Awareness Training (HEAT). People in Need expects all staff to perform job duties and responsibilities in accordance with People in Need code of conduct and key policies (available at: https://www.peopleinneed.net/key-policies-4142gp ). review_candidates.title: Corporate Affairs Officer
review_candidates.description: SUMMARY: Job Title: Corporate Affairs Officer Contract Type: Full time Reports to: Head of Corporate Affairs Location: Central London, with occasional international travel. Hybrid working: A minimum of three days per week in the office, with home-working arrangements at the discretion of the CEO. Hours: 9:30am–5:30pm, Monday to Friday, with occasional breakfast and evening events. Salary: £30,000–£35,000 per annum, depending on skills and experience. Annual leave: 25 working days per year, plus Bank Holidays. Benefits: Contributory pension, health insurance, season ticket loan and language classes (Spanish, English or Portuguese). THE ORGANISATION: Canning House (CH) is the United Kingdom’s leading forum on Latin America. For over 80 years, its mission has been to build understanding and relationships between the UK, Latin America & Iberia. The organisation convenes high-level conferences, seminars and roundtables; publishes insightful reports, white papers and blogs; and maintains an extensive senior network among businesses, experts and influencers, all across the broadest range of subjects, sectors and specialisms. THE ROLE: Canning House is seeking a proactive, highly organised and personable Corporate Affairs Officer to support the development and management of its relationships with commercial organisations and other key stakeholders. These include existing and prospective corporate members, sponsors, Trade Promotion Organisations (TPOs), multinationals and other organisations with an interest in Latin America and Iberia, as well as the region's political, economic and current affairs. Reporting to the Head of Corporate Affairs , the Corporate Affairs Officer will play an important role in delivering Canning House's corporate engagement strategy, strengthening relationships with stakeholders and supporting the growth, engagement and retention of the organisation's corporate membership. This is a varied and outward-facing role, combining relationship management, business development, event delivery, stakeholder engagement and administration. The successful candidate will be comfortable engaging with senior external stakeholders, managing multiple priorities and taking ownership of projects from conception through to delivery. The role would suit someone who is commercially minded, highly organised and genuinely interested in Latin America, Iberia and international affairs. KEY RESPONIBILITIES Corporate Membership and Stakeholder Engagement Build and maintain strong, professional relationships with corporate members, prospective members, sponsors and other stakeholders. Support the recruitment of new corporate members and the retention and engagement of existing members. Maintain regular, effective and professional communication with Canning House's corporate network. Identify opportunities to increase corporate members' engagement with Canning House's events, publications, thought leadership and other activities. Support the delivery of membership growth and engagement targets. Assist with the preparation of membership proposals, presentations and other corporate engagement materials. Maintain accurate and up-to-date membership records, databases and CRM information. Events and Programmes Support the planning and delivery of Canning House events and programmes for corporate members and other stakeholders, including: Identifying, inviting and coordinating speakers and panellists. Preparing invitations, briefing notes, agendas and supporting materials. Coordinating venues, guest lists, registrations and event logistics. Liaising professionally with speakers, sponsors, members, partners and suppliers. Supporting event promotion and communications. Assisting with event delivery, including occasional early morning and evening events. Conducting post-event follow-up and identifying opportunities for further stakeholder engagement. Supporting the development of new event concepts and programme ideas. Sponsorship and Business Development Assist with identifying and developing sponsorship opportunities for events, publications and other Canning House activities. Support the preparation of sponsorship proposals and presentations. Help identify potential commercial partners and opportunities for collaboration. Maintain professional relationships with existing and prospective sponsors and partners. Corporate Affairs and Research Prepare correspondence, presentations, briefings, reports and other materials for corporate engagement. Monitor relevant political, economic and business developments in Latin America and identify issues of potential interest to Canning House and its corporate network. Contribute ideas and insights to Canning House's corporate engagement and programme development. Represent Canning House professionally at meetings, events and external engagements. Teamwork and Administration Work collaboratively with colleagues across Canning House to support the organisation's wider objectives. Ensure corporate and event-related information is recorded accurately and efficiently. Support general administrative and operational requirements associated with the Corporate Affairs function. Undertake other duties reasonably required to support the objectives of the role and Canning House. PERSON SPECIFICATION: Essential The successful candidate will demonstrate: A collegiate, collaborative and team-oriented approach. Reliability, professionalism, sound judgement and a strong sense of responsibility. Initiative, creativity and the ability to develop and implement new ideas. Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver work to agreed deadlines. Confidence and professionalism when engaging with external stakeholders, including senior business representatives. Excellent written and spoken English, with strong attention to detail. Strong administrative, coordination and project-management skills. Good proficiency in Microsoft Office and CRM systems. The ability to work independently, take ownership of tasks and follow projects through to completion. A positive, flexible and solutions-oriented approach. Respect for colleagues, stakeholders and the values of the organisation. Knowledge of, or a genuine curiosity about, Latin America and Iberia, together with a willingness to deepen knowledge of the region. The legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Desirable The following would be advantageous but are not essential: Experience working with corporate organisations, membership organisations, chambers of commerce, public affairs, professional services, government or international organisations. Previous experience in relationship management, business development, events, sponsorship or stakeholder engagement. Professional experience or a strong academic background relating to Latin America or Iberia. Spanish and/or Portuguese language skills. Experience working in an international or multicultural environment. A university degree or equivalent qualification, preferably in International Relations, International Affairs, International Business, Trade, Public Relations, Communications, Latin American Studies or a related discipline. HOW AND APPLY: If you meet the requirements and are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Canning House’s work, please send your CV and covering letter to the Head of Corporate Affairs at corporate@canninghouse.org by Friday, 2 October 2026. Interviews: Tuesday, 6 October 2026, and Thursday, 8 October 2026.

Automate data collection and consolidation from HR trackers into standardized dashboards, reducing manual reporting. Establish simple data standards and validation processes to improve data quality and consistency. Provide monthly workforce and manpower insights to support management decisions. Maintain a central reference of multi-country benefits and statutory requirements to support workforce planning and staff cost forecasting. Manpower Forecasting & Budgeting Develop robust headcount and labour cost forecasting models aligned with organisational growth plans. Monitor actual manpower costs against budget and highlight key variances and trends. Collaborate with other HR functions and Finance to understand cost movements and recommend actions. HR Management Systems (HRMS) Support HRMS upgrades, enhancements, UAT and system improvements. Investigate system issues, data discrepancies and integration errors, working with vendors to resolve them. Collaborate with other HR functions to identify opportunities to improve and automate HR processes and reporting. Develop user guides, SOPs and data governance practices to support effective system usage. Market Research & Benchmarking Partner closely with the HR Operations & Rewards team to conduct market research and benchmarking studies on salary benchmarks, market movements, and increment trends across various jurisdictions. Stakeholder & Vendor Engagement Work closely with HR, Finance and other stakeholders to gather, validate and interpret data. THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT Education At least a Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Finance, Data Analytics, Information Systems, Engineering or a related discipline. Technical and Professional Knowledge Experience developing HR dashboards, management reports and workforce analytics. Expertise in financial modeling, headcount forecasting, and actual vs. budget variance analysis. Hands-on experience in HRMS implementation, UAT, system enhancement, troubleshooting and data management. Advanced Excel, with knowledge of Power Query, Power BI or similar tools Sound understanding of HR frameworks, multi-country benefits and statutory requirements Other Special Requirements Ability to handle highly confidential executive compensation and headcount data with extreme discretion and integrity. Functional Competencies Highly Analytical: Ability to analyse complex information, connect the dots and turn data into meaningful insights and recommendations. Behavioral Competencies Unity in Diversity: Values diverse perspectives and works inclusively across cultures and teams. Communication & Collaboration: Communicates openly, collaborates effectively and provides responsive, service-oriented support. Innovation & Continuous Improvement: Is proactive, embraces change and continuously seeks better ways of working. Accountability: Takes ownership, works independently and adapts to changing priorities. Integrity & Trust: Acts with honesty, transparency and professionalism, building trust through reliable delivery.
